chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) claiming a debt from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays. He said, 'He has taken my right.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'It is the one who killed him that has taken your right.' Then he said to Al-Walid, 'Stand up to the man and pay him from his right, for I wish to cool his skin which was already cold.'
ai.seo_question: How are debts handled when a person dies without paying them, according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the principle of *qada* (debt settlement) from the deceased's estate, using the metaphor of 'cooling the skin' to signify alleviating the spiritual burden of unpaid debts in the afterlife. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of financial obligations after death and the merit of settling debts to ensure the deceased's peace. The instruction to Walid ibn Sabih to pay directly underscores the practical implementation of this right by the Imam or his representatives.
